newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Binariang to raise up to 1.5 bln rgt.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Binariang to raise up to 1.5 bln rgt.

text.p: Malaysian telecommunications firm Binariang Sdn Bhd said on Thursday it hopes to raise between 1.0 billion and 1.5 billion ringgit by the third quarter of 1997 to cover the expansion of its mobile telephony system.
Chan Chee Beng, Binariang's executive director, told reporters following a presentation to fund managers that the funds would be raised through selling bonds or stocks.
"We would be looking to sell bonds," he said. "We can either look at the banking market or the capital market."
He added, "We would be looking to raise 1-1.5 billion ringgit."
He said the company would complete its review of the proposed flotation exercise by the end of second quarter 1997 and would go to the market by the third quarter.

"We are looking to double our investment in the GSM network from 500 million to 1.0 billion ringgit and that is the kind of ballpark that we would be looking for," he said. GSM is the world's most commonly used global digital cellular mobile network.
A flotation exercise would dilute the ownership of U.S. West International, which currently holds a 20 percent stake in Binariang, Chan said.
"If we sell 20 percent of the enlarged capital (in an initial public offering), U.S. West's stake would fall from 20 percent to 16 percent," he said.
U.S. West is Binariang's foreign partner which has been responsible for transferring the technology it needed to launch Malaysia's first two telecommunications satellites.
Binariang, whose Malaysian owner is tycoon T. Ananda Krishnan, is involved in mobile telephony, direct-to-user satellite TV, fixed-line telephony and international gateway services.

Chan also said during his presentation at the infrastructure conference that the two satellites which it launched in 1996 would be able to recover their costs in seven years' time and generate an internal revenue rate of 15 to 17 percent per year.

Binariang also said it expects its GSM to attract 700,000 subscribers by the year 2000 and 500,000 for its fixed-lined network. That compares with 150,000 GSM and 5,000 fixed-line customers currently.
Chan also said that the company hopes to have 80,000 to 100,000 fixed lines running through 250,000 homes throughout Malaysia by the end of 1997.
